Location:This role is fully remote and open only to candidates based in Latin America. We're not able to consider candidates based in the US or other regions for this position. Our dev team works on Eastern Time (ET).
How we build
We don't type code. Our engineers work through agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) and most of what ships is agent-written. You describe the outcome, the agent plans and implements, the agent reviews its own work, and then you review it.
The first and the last steps are the job. You set the shape before the agent builds, and you're the first human to read what comes back. You own every line that lands in production. Whole-team PR review sits on top of that, not instead of it. "The agent wrote it" never explains a bug here.
Company accounts for Claude, Codex and Cursor are provided and you're expected to use them hard. No token budget to ration.
What you'll do

- Ship merchant-facing features end to end, from data model to API to UI, directing agents through the whole path

- Decide the shape before the agent builds it: where a boundary goes, what's sync vs. queued, what the contract is, what gets denormalized

- Catch what the agent got wrong: the plausible-looking query that doesn't scale, the missing failure path, the abstraction that will cost us in six months

- Make agent output verifiable with tests that define done, contracts that hold, and changes that can be rolled back

- Bring new tooling and workflows into the team when you find something better

What we're looking for
Web development and web services architecture. That's the bar, not a specific language.

- 3+ years building and running production web applications

- You reason fluently about client-server, sync vs. async, scheduling and background work, caching, and failure modes, and you can explain a decision to an agent well enough that it builds the right thing

- Architectural patterns are working tools for you, not vocabulary: MVC, layered, hexagonal, DDD, and the code-level patterns underneath. You know when each is worth it and when it's overhead

- Strong SQL and relational data modeling. Non-negotiable

- You instrument what you ship. Production observability and performance tooling (Datadog, New Relic, Sentry or similar) is how you find out the agent's code actually works

- Daily production use of coding agents. You ship with them, you're not evaluating them

- You can take a codebase you didn't write and an agent's plan for changing it, and tell whether the plan is right

Any language. PHP/Laravel and JavaScript/Vue are a plus. That's our current stack and you'll be in it week one, with agents to get you there.
Also a plus: LLM APIs in production, e-commerce platforms (Shopify, fulfillment), queues and event-driven work, MCP servers or custom agent skills.
Interview process

- Intro with our HR Manager

- Technical conversation with a Tech Lead and the CTO. Expect to review real agent-generated code and defend architectural calls

- Conversation with the CTO of our parent company

The Role
Crimson is replacing Salesforce with Salesflow, an AI-native CRM we build in-house. It runs the whole sales journey: lead intake, meeting scheduling, call transcription analysis, AI-drafted appraisals, contracts and e-signature, and invoicing. It is live for our US sales team today and rolls out to every other market over the coming months.
Our team is small and builder-heavy, and the rate of growth has made it hard to keep the underlying infrastructure and logic clean and tidy. As examples, CI checks things that have been fully deprecated, newly added modules do not always take into account legacy compatibility, and bug fixes are sometimes too narrow in scope, fixing the place the problem was seen and not the underlying cause. Compounding the above is that the code itself is for the most part written by AI – this is what enabled us to build a fully working CRM in a matter of months, but is what makes it very easy to inadvertently cross wires during development.
We are looking for the person who fixes this: you will own the backend view of the system as a whole and maintain the code that glues everything together. That means a system inventory and state transition models, CI that tests only what is needed and does that well, shared guarded entrypoints in place of multiple writers with inconsistent guards, and clear definitions for what is the source of truth when fields are shared among multiple synced systems. Salesflow is live and people depend on it every day, so this is done in steps while it runs: there is no rewrite. This is not a hands-off design role: you will be expected to push code as well as design.
In addition to the above, you'll also help to unblock users – the support team funnel tickets that prevent a user from working and require a backend code change to the dev team, most of whom are not in US time zones. You will join the team and cover the US working day, when the other members are offline.
We fully expect you to use AI to augment your analyses and write code for you but absolutely require that you have the experience to read and write code yourself, and that you know how to use AI to write code (e.g., which questions to ask, what to check, how to build internal memory structures).
What are the main responsibilities for this role?
Your top priority is to build and maintain the view of the CRM as a whole: inventory all functions, edge functions, flows, and integrations with outside systems; build the state transition map and the set of business rules the system is held to; and then ensure that architecture and CI align to this. In practice this can be split into:

- setting up a live and auto-updating inventory and model: the repo has multiple pushes every day; no-one should try updating a model by hand

- coordinating with team members on business rules: the team has, collectively, all the info; your job is to organize it and embed it in the checks

- after the above two, move into implementation: resolve technical debt caused by rapid organic growth without consistent pruning, and set up the infrastructure such that future growth automatically falls into the correct path and does not create new debt.

Aside from this, you will assist in unblocking users during US daytime hours: addressing current bugs will help you gain insight into the system as a whole, informing the main priority.

- Your first 28 days: start shipping basic sanitation: clean CI and updated CLAUDE.md files (the instructions our AI agents read) so future pushes don't create more problems

- Your first 3 months: the worst of the debt is cleared and guardrails are in place, so a bug that has been fixed does not come back; your time will transition over to building new features

What skills and experience are required?

Product engineering at Descript means owning outcomes, not just tickets — you'll take a problem from a rough idea to a shipped, measured result, working closely with product, design, and the rest of engineering along the way. We organize around a few teams, each responsible for a distinct part of the product:

- Editor: owns our video editor. Help make traditionally complex video-editing workflows simpler, craft cutting-edge AI into practical creative tools, and build on our vision of turning a text-editor for video into a tool that puts video in everyone's communication toolkit.

- Growth & Monetization: owns onboarding and activation, growth loops and in-product experiments, plans and pricing, checkout, billing, and AI credits. Help turn visitors into customers and customers into revenue.

- Media: owns upload, transcription, diarization, alignment, drive-wide search, playback, rendering, and export (including the engine we're rewriting in Rust ). Help make media fast to bring in, easy to find, instant to play, and reliable to export.

- Agent: owns Underlord, Descript’s AI co-editor. Build the representations, tools, harness, evals, and feedback loops that let it reason about video projects, make edits, and check its work. Help people and agents collaborate naturally, whether in the editor or through our API and MCP.

- Identity & Access (aka TACO): owns login, authentication and authorization, account settings, and project organization, plus the enterprise layer of workspaces, SSO/SCIM, governance, and audit logs. Help individuals become teams, and teams scale into enterprises, with the trust and security to go all in.

What You’ll Do

- Own meaningful product surfaces end to end. Take problems from definition through design, implementation, launch, measurement, and maintenance. Improve core Editor workflows, shape the self-serve journey from signup through renewal, or help make Underlord more sentient.

- Shape the product, not just the implementation. Partner with Product and Design to propose better interactions, expose constraints, choose the right metrics, and find simpler paths to user outcomes.

- Build ambitious full-stack systems with care. Create responsive, reliable experiences. Stretch from TypeScript and React to NodeJS and Temporal to first and third party integrations to get the job done.

- Improve how the team learns and ships. Form hypotheses, instrument your work, release incrementally, and read results honestly. Strengthen the tooling, standards, tests, observability, and release practices that help the team move quickly without compromising quality.

- Raise the team’s technical ambition. Provide architectural direction, thoughtful reviews, mentoring, and clear human writing.

- You create clarity in ambiguous work and can navigate (and simplify!) significant product and technical complexity.

- You validate your work rigorously through focused reproductions, logs, tests, and other evidence rather than trusting that the output looks right.

Sobre Creai
En Creai , nos especializamos en aprovechar el poder de la inteligencia artificial y el aprendizaje automático para transformar negocios. Nuestra misión es ayudar a los clientes a reducir costos, aumentar la eficiencia y desbloquear nuevas oportunidades mediante soluciones de IA de vanguardia.
Descripción del Puesto
Como Full Stack Software Engineer para IA, tu rol central ya no es escribir código línea por línea, sino dirigir, supervisar y validar el trabajo de agentes de IA generativa y agentica que construyen soluciones escalables y de alto impacto. Usarás tu dominio técnico y de negocio para diseñar la arquitectura correcta, definir el qué y el por qué de cada solución, delegar la ejecución táctica a la IA , y ejercer el criterio necesario para juzgar, corregir y aprobar sus outputs antes de que lleguen a producción.

Serás responsable de entregar funcionalidades completas de complejidad alta con velocidad y calidad, asegurando que la velocidad que da la IA no comprometa la estabilidad, seguridad ni mantenibilidad del sistema. Colaborarás con otros ingenieros y equipos multidisciplinarios para integrar servicios, pipelines y modelos, fortaleciendo los estándares técnicos y las prácticas de supervisión de IA dentro de Creai .

Este Puesto Exige

- Orquestación de Desarrollo: Dirigir a agentes de IA para generar funciones y servicios, revisando y refactorizando el código resultante para garantizar que sea limpio, funcional, mantenible y esté alineado con la arquitectura del sistema. Escribir código propio cuando la tarea lo requiera, especialmente en piezas críticas o ambiguas donde el criterio humano marca la diferencia.

- Validación de Calidad: Diseñar la estrategia de pruebas (smoke tests, integración, end to end etc) y delegar su automatización a IA, verificando que la cobertura generada realmente valide los casos de negocio relevantes y no solo los casos evidentes.

- Gestión de Datos: Definir la arquitectura de pipelines batch de datos y usar IA para acelerar su construcción, auditando personalmente la validación de schemas y la coherencia entre orígenes y destinos, dado que los errores de datos introducidos por IA suelen ser sutiles y costosos de detectar tarde.

- Modelado y Entrenamiento Inicial: Supervisar el entrenamiento de modelos estándar y el ajuste de hiperparámetros —ejecutado manualmente o asistido por IA— bajo la guía del equipo de IA, evaluando de forma crítica si los resultados obtenidos responden al problema de negocio planteado.

- Gestión de Incidentes: Usar IA para acelerar el triage y diagnóstico de incidentes, manteniendo la responsabilidad final de clasificar, comunicar y resolver runbooks comunes, y aportando criterio en los casos que la IA no puede resolver por sí sola.

- Seguridad del Software: Usar IA para ejecutar threat checklists y sugerir parches, validando y priorizando esas recomendaciones con criterio propio antes de aplicarlas, evitando falsos positivos o negativos que la IA no puede juzgar por contexto de negocio.
